newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE sets out derivatives strategy under EMU.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE sets out derivatives strategy under EMU.

text.p: The London Internatioanal Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) on Tuesday set out a four-point strategy for realising its aim of becoming the world centre for derivatives under a European single currency.
Among the main points, LIFFE said it would look to build alliances with other exchanges.
"There will be fierce competition for new futures and options contracts that will emerge after European Monetary Union (EMU) is established," said LIFFE chairman Jack Wigglesworth in a statement.

LIFFE also said it would urge the British government to keep its options open on EMU for as long as possible. "For the UK and Europe, British influence in the detailed EMU negotiations should be maximised," the exchange said.
It said even if Britain were to opt out of EMU in 1999, it made sense to leave any announcement as long as possible to avoid any diminuation of British influence.
LIFFE said the main elements of its strategy were --
-- reviewing and enhancing the range of contracts,
-- reinforcing the strengths of its trading platform,
-- building a network of strategic alliances with other exchanges,
-- and underpinning its position as a well regulated exchange with high standards.
"We believe that we have the strengths and strategy to seize the opportunities EMU brings, regrardless of whether or not the UK participates," Wigglesworth said.

LIFFE said the first steps have already been taken. "LIFFE's Euromark has been developed to become, in effect, the first short-term interest rate future to be explicitly denominated in euros after EMU begins."

The exchange said the contract is securing most business for maturites beyond January 1, 1999. "For example, the Euromark, which expires in March 1999, has traded since its launch five times as many contracts as its French equivalent," it said.
